column1: # The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2), base dump. Nintendo SDK 22.2.8, NVN2.

column2: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

column1: # The NPDM declares 48 MiB of system resources. Startup requests a 6.20 GiB heap.
# The alias region holds the game's streaming allocator (main+0x7ed630): in Kokiri Forest it keeps about 5,100 address regions with 3.0-3.3 GB mapped, spread up to
# +4.95 GB (DM_REGIONS). With 2.38 GB (0x98000000) VammManager::AllocateAddressRegion failed after 5-15 minutes outdoors and the game aborted (nn::diag abort,
# Result 0, sdk+0x16cb54). 8 GB leaves room for its fragmentation; the reserve grows by the same 5.6 GB so the heap keeps its size
# A map that would take the process past the application pool fails with ResultLimitReached, as on Horizon: the SDK's allocator keeps freed pages mapped until a map fails,
# then gives them back. Without it PR #1444 reports crashes entering Hyrule Castle, Kakariko Village and Death Mountain and a black screen leaving the Deku Tree
# agl wraps its depth clears in render conditions, as on Donkey Kong Bananza and Splatoon Raiders: in Kokiri Forest the main opaque pass tests EQUAL against a copy of the prepass depth
# that a conditional clear (skipped on the console) wiped first, so no lit geometry landed and the full-screen sky showed through everywhere (a white scene)
# Pool tables (shaders reading textures through handles cover every registered ID, about 33,000) made a texture again for each ID whose texture the game had finalized: at the
# house-to-forest change 1,500 textures and 2.5 GB held only by retired IDs, as much again in deferred release, 16 GB GPU allocated and out of GPU memory. Retired IDs get the dummy
# The game's compute dispatches with no barrier of its between them run side by side (nvn_mtl.m dispatch_enc): 117 at the start of a frame in Kokiri Forest waited each for the one
# before, 5.7 ms; side by side 3.7 ms, the frame 27.1 -> 24.9 ms (docked, Apple M4 Pro), the picture within run-to-run noise
# Frame rate limiter (patches.py fps_limit, from cheemu21's kid-with-sword-remake): the launcher's Frame rate offers the game's own step (0, the default) and 30. At 30 the
# game's own 30 fps mode (interval 2) holds every frame two vsyncs at full game speed. 0 runs as A1 and Mighty Green Kokiri Kid v3 did: the game picks its own interval and
# real_speed's measured step keeps the speed. A2's default of 60 put the host's frame step (hle_nvn.c fstep_tick) in charge of every frame, and ran far worse on the iPhone
# Render scale (patches.py render_scale): the 3D views fixed at this fraction of the output, the dynamic resolution off. 0.75 draws 960x540 in handheld's 1280x720
# (DM_GFX_SCALE=2), the Mighty Green Kokiri Kid fork's iPhone setting; the launcher's Render scale slider moves it from 0.5 to 1.0 (1.0 = the game's own dynamic resolution)
# The launcher's Preset: Potato (loader.c dm_preset_apply) for phones with less memory, aimed at a GPU memory peak under 5 GB (Standard peaks at 5.6 GB in Kokiri Forest on the Mac and
# the v3 author's iPhone). Render scale 0.6 (the launcher locks the slider); cheemu21's softer textures (large 2D game textures without their finest level, made whole again when the
# game reads one back) beside DM_NVN_TEX_MIP_SKIP's 1024; lossy render targets; large pools wired by chunk (gmem_nobig, -730 MB on the Mac); the guard lets go of idle textures from
# 4,400 MB; a smaller recycle bin and a quicker sweep of unused shared textures. DM_NVN_TEX_MIP_SKIP=512 froze the game after the save loaded (Mac), so it is not here.
# Not yet measured as a whole
# The iPhone's touch gamepad starts in the Native layout (kid-with-sword-remake): translucent keys with icons and letter chips, a floating left stick and the camera on
# any drag of the right half. 2D, 3D and Tap stay in the in-game menu
# The touch controls' Forest colours: blue A, green B, yellow X / Y, red +, deep green shoulders, bronze D-pad, gold rims, all translucent (DmGamepad.m theme_init)
